newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler leads list of largest German firms.
newsitem.headline: Daimler leads list of largest German firms.

text.p: Car maker Daimler-Benz AG again topped the list of largest German corporations, but industrial group Siemens AG was the most profitable, business daily Handelsblatt reported Monday.

Daimler-Benz, with 1996 sales of 106 billion marks ($61 billion), was followed in the top five by Volkswagen AG, Siemens, utility group Veba AG and Deutsche Telekom AG, according to Handelsblatt's annual ranking.
The same firms made up the top five in 1995 when Siemens was ranked second and VW third.

In net profit, Siemens outpaced all others with 2.99 billion marks ($1.7 billion). Chemicals makers BASF AG, Hoechst AG and Bayer AG were second, third and fifth, respectively, with Daimler ranking fourth in net profit.
Veba and Telekom were sixth and seven in profit, while VW stood well down on the profit ladder with 678 million marks.
Siemens was the largest employer with 379,000 workers worldwide, followed by Daimler-Benz, national railroad Deutsche Bahn AG, the post office Deutsche Post AG and VW.

Handelsblatt said troubled consumer electronics group Grundig and Ford Motor Co. Ford Werke suffered the largest losses -- 553 million marks ($318 million) and 552 million marks ($317 million), respectively.
